title: Archive Fraction contribution-table feasibility and negative complete-cost screen
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Archive a scoped negative result for the frozen PR #5848 Fraction error trace: primitive profiling and an exact bounded contribution table pass the recorded correctness checks, but the complete-cost screen does not justify complete qualifier construction. The package preserves both table versions, proof, finite replay, full actual audit receipts, profile data and the stopping decision in `research/fraction-contribution-table-feasibility`.

The final single ordered trace comparison is 20.251 → 14.600 seconds. Adding the observed new finite-check cost to the existing complete-stage baseline gives a **modelled 34.984 seconds / 10.33% saving**, below the required 15% screen. This is not a measured complete wall/CPU result, performance submission, universal obstruction, paid-profile improvement or κ gain. No complete qualifier or complete B/C benchmark was constructed. Frozen source and the independent integer oracle remain unchanged.

## Task and overlap

- Task `replay-runtime`; scope **refined** to `PR5848/frozen-66fb6c6/Fraction-primitives-and-bounded-contribution-table` for profiling and feasibility before construction.
- Canonical main / priority-8 guidance: `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`; submitted head: `df9dc4c89b31494f1390d16b9ca2a15e5946e853`.
- Frozen PR #5848 input: `66fb6c6b8683b37967e9d7f313b3df99a49d2406`, complete 97-file export including unchanged PR #5831/#5826 archives and notices; immutable input ancestor `0b2de67914ff659b0e1fca4ff4f275228aa246d6`.
- Retained test-only dependency from Ali Romman's PR #5761: cherry-pick `01014cbe772ea5a59ccbc55266222433944c7368` (`test: retain frozen research routes across priority revisions`). Its three files are included alongside the 66-file research package. No test suite is weakened here.
- Nearest work: [PR #5848](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5848), [zero/unit negative finding](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5848#issuecomment-6435104002) at `71f22c77b393e5cc14925c771894dc1a92c8443c`, and [canonical profile/table handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5848#issuecomment-6435652427). The added value is an exact local-table correctness argument, primitive census, retained actual audits and an explicit complete-cost stop decision.

The earlier handoff and frozen package say no performance PR was opened after the screen. This submission now archives the scoped negative finding at the donor's explicit request; it does not reopen the performance claim or change historical evidence.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only. Recorded evidence, rather than fresh numerical reruns for publication:

- 241 finite programs / 10,164 events at capacities 0, 1, 2 and 16,384: **964 complete value/witness/type/input comparisons**; all **34** key, collision, capacity, eviction, exception, source, mutation and restoration controls pass normally and under optimization.
- Two full actual trace audits retain every returned value/type/witness/input across **25,984 events / 799 coordinates**. These are single ordered within-process observations, not medians, CPU gains or a causal separation of capacity/container effects.
- All ten guarded commands passed in **179.502 seconds**, within the recorded original 180-second command cap, 600-second initial / 1,500-second shared cap, 1 GiB sampled process-group RSS and zero automatic retries. Portable packaged finite replay passed normally and under `-O`; source/export bytes and modes stayed unchanged.
- Full complete-candidate normal/O/sealed/hosted performance gates were deliberately not started after the negative screen. This PR's hosted CI status must be read separately at its exact head; no hosted pass is inferred from local receipts. Full-history preflight was unavailable in the shallow checkout.

Fresh finite-only reproduction (about 1.6–2.9 seconds on the recorded host):

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/fraction-contribution-table-feasibility
```

The manifest explicitly declares finite-only coverage. `actual_audit.py` is separately opt-in and needs a fresh serial budget; historical profiling/audits need not be repeated to acknowledge this archival handoff.

## Credit

Ali Romman supplied the original Fraction/error arithmetic and integer backend. Preserve PR #5831, #5826, #5819, Adam Gall, ywz65, PR #2878, Mason Hale / PR #5811 and all retained P104/native/compiler/precision notices. PR #5848 / #5839 supply the qualifier/Linux baseline; PR #5816, #5818, #5832 and Ali Romman's exact test-only PR #5761 retain tooling, authorship and cherry-pick credit. The preceding zero/unit artifact supplies source-binding and fixture lineage. Memoization is standard.

New profile/table/feasibility work: Chris R / Clear1nsight with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. The frozen experiment used no subagents; this publication audit is agent-assisted. No independent human/kernel acceptance is claimed. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

See the package README and TASK.json. The smallest separately assigned follow-up is to establish a source-bound well-formed Fraction contract and internal type preservation before considering relocation of the new table's repeated type checks, with malformed-input fallback and all controls retained. Its cost and possible gain remain unmeasured. No successor research is dispatched by this archival submission; κ research, Work 1/2, feeds and automations remain paused.
